name: Louisiana
note: In Louisiana the funeral director files the death certificate with the parish local registrar within five days, and always before disposition. The attending physician must certify the cause within 24 hours. The parish coroner takes unattended, suspicious and violent deaths, and any death more than ten days after the decedent last saw a physician. A burial-transit permit from the local registrar gates disposition, but it does not need a completed certificate except for removal from the continental United States. The local registrar keeps the original for ten days and then forwards it to the state registrar. Each month the state registrar notifies parish registrars of voters, and the Louisiana Department of Health sends the Department of State a monthly death report for voter cancellation. No other statutory onward feed was found. Certified copies go only to the persons listed in R.S. 40:41, which include insurance, pension, retirement and payable-on-death beneficiaries.

steps.title: Physician's announced opinion of death
steps.who: A physician licensed in Louisiana. For organ transplants, an additional physician not on the transplant team (or one under a written hospital policy).
steps.trigger: Irreversible cessation of respiratory and circulatory functions, or of total brain function.
steps.summary: Louisiana makes death turn on a physician's 'announced opinion'.

steps.title: Coroner pronounces on reports from nurses, PAs or EMTs at the scene
steps.who: Coroner investigators, registered or licensed practical nurses, physician assistants or emergency medical technicians at the scene, reporting what they observed first-hand.
steps.trigger: A death outside a physician's presence.
steps.summary: The coroner may pronounce death on these reports. The time of death is recorded as when it was reported or discovered.

steps.title: Notify the coroner of sudden, violent, suspicious or unattended deaths
steps.who: A physician or any other person who knows of the death. An undertaker or embalmer must notify and get the coroner's permission before moving or preparing the body.
steps.trigger: A sudden, accidental, violent or suspicious death, or one without medical attendance in the preceding 24 hours.
steps.summary: Failure is a misdemeanor with a fine of up to $5,000. The coroner must view the body or investigate in the listed categories, including bodies found dead and natural deaths within 24 hours of hospital admission.

steps.title: Funeral director takes personal data from the best-qualified person
steps.who: The person best qualified to supply the personal data.
steps.trigger: The funeral director preparing the certificate.
steps.summary: The funeral director, or person acting as such, prepares and files the certificate.

steps.title: Attending physician certifies the cause within 24 hours
steps.who: The physician last in attendance. Alternatively an associate, the institution's chief medical officer, the autopsy physician or the coroner (natural deaths only).
steps.trigger: Presentation of the certificate by the funeral director.
steps.summary: If the cause cannot be determined within 48 hours, the funeral director must be told why. Disposition then waits for authorisation by the physician or coroner.

steps.title: Local registrar refers unattended or long-unattended deaths to the coroner
steps.who: The local registrar, after the funeral director reports that the death was unattended or that the physician will not sign.
steps.trigger: No medical attendance, physician refusal, apparently non-natural causes, or death more than ten days after last treatment by a physician.

deadline.text: before issuing a permit for disposition

steps.summary: The coroner determines the cause and signs the medical certification within 48 hours of taking charge.

steps.title: Funeral director files the original certificate with the parish local registrar
steps.who: The funeral director or person acting as such. Local registrars are Office of Public Health employees in each parish health unit. The state registrar serves Orleans.

deadline.text: within five days after its occurrence, and before any disposition

steps.summary: Wilful neglect of a duty in the chapter is punishable by a fine of up to $1,000, up to one year's imprisonment, or both.

steps.title: Burial-transit permit from the local registrar
steps.trigger: A request to inter, entomb, cremate, remove or otherwise dispose of the body.
steps.summary: The permit does not require a completed death certificate, except for removal from the continental United States. Moving a body without a permit is an offence.

steps.title: Local registrar forwards the certificate to the state registrar on day ten
steps.who: The parish local registrar, to the state registrar (Vital Records Registry, Office of Public Health).

deadline.text: on the tenth day after the certificate is filed

steps.summary: During the ten days the local registrar may correct non-medical items and issue certified copies.

steps.title: Certified copies to listed applicants only
steps.who: The state registrar, the local registrar (during the first ten days), and the clerks of district court and the Second City Court of New Orleans. Eligible applicants: the registrant, immediate or surviving family, insurance or trust beneficiaries, succession representatives, legatees, public-pension, retirement-plan and payable-on-death beneficiaries, and attorneys for any of them.

deadline.text: within ten business days of the state registrar receiving the request

steps.summary: Copies are restricted to the persons listed in R.S. 40:41(C). Clerks of court are bound by the same eligibility rules.

steps.title: State registrar notifies parish registrars of voters monthly
steps.who: The state registrar, to each parish registrar of voters.
steps.trigger: Death certificates received for residents over 18.
steps.summary: The notice gives the name, address and age of each deceased adult resident of the parish.

steps.title: LDH monthly death report to the Department of State
steps.who: The secretary of the Louisiana Department of Health, to the Department of State (Secretary of State).
steps.trigger: Deaths of persons aged 16 or over in the preceding month.

deadline.text: by the tenth day of each month; cancellation within thirty days of receipt

steps.summary: The Department of State cancels registrations that match its criteria exactly and tells the parish registrar. Non-matches go to parish registrars to review within 30 days.

steps.title: Removal on a certified copy or an obituary
steps.who: Anyone presenting a certified copy. Registrars must also search obituaries.
steps.trigger: Receipt of a certified copy of a death certificate, or an obituary identifying the voter.

deadline.text: within thirty days after receipt of a certified copy

steps.summary: The parish registrar of voters must remove the name. Obituaries that identify the voter well enough must also be used to cancel.

steps.title: Beneficiaries and family present certified copies to insurers and banks
steps.who: The family, the succession representative, or a named beneficiary of an insurance policy, pension, retirement plan or payable-on-death account.
steps.summary: Beneficiaries may get certified copies in their own right. No statute was found that lets banks or insurers verify deaths directly, or that requires them to check.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Within five days of death and in any case before disposition.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director or person acting as such prepares and files. The informant supplies personal data.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: Parish coroners investigate referred categories only: unattended, suspicious, violent, more than ten days since last treatment, or within 24 hours of hospital admission. There is no review of every certificate.

electronicRegistration.note: Statute recognises electronic records and signatures but does not mandate electronic filing, and the process is framed around a paper original kept for ten days by the local registrar. LDH material on the Louisiana Electronic Vital Records System could not be read (ldh.la.gov blocked).

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register. The central vital records registry is an event register.

governmentPropagation.note: Statute requires automatic death notices only to registrars of voters and the Department of State. No statutory feed to the Office of Motor Vehicles, Medicaid or the Department of Revenue was found. Federal feeds are in the us-federal layer.

certificateAccess.note: Only the registrant, family, beneficiaries (insurance, trust, public pension, retirement, payable-on-death), succession representatives, legatees, bail-bond sureties and their attorneys may get copies.

privateSectorVerification.note: No official verification route for banks or insurers was found. They rely on certified copies presented by eligible beneficiaries or the family.

gaps: ldh.la.gov and www.ldh.la.gov are blocked by egress policy (CONNECT 403), so LDH Vital Records pages on the Louisiana Electronic Vital Records System, copy eligibility and fees could not be read.
The LDH vital records regulations (LAC Title 48) were not read. They may mandate electronic filing (R.S. 40:38 refers to regulations for copies).

No statute was found requiring LDH to notify the Office of Motor Vehicles (driver licences), Louisiana Medicaid or the Department of Revenue. Title 32 and Title 46 index descriptions were scanned for 'deceased' and 'death'; only R.S. 32:707.1 (vehicle titles of deceased persons) appeared.
Whether Louisiana sends deaths to SSA through electronic death registration is not stated in Title 40. That is left to the us-federal layer.

R.S. 40:41(A) says certificates are 'open to inspection, subject to the provisions of this Chapter', but (C) then restricts inspection and copies to listed persons. certificateAccess is recorded as restricted on that basis.
Coroner duties formerly at R.S. 33:1561 ff. were redesignated to R.S. 13:5711 ff. by Acts 2011, No. 248. The current Title 13 sections are cited.
